albums.blurb: Rodrigo Sánchez and Gabriela Quintero are a Mexico City duo who started out in a thrash-metal band before moving to Dublin to busk, and this self-titled record — produced by John Leckie and released on Rubyworks in February 2006 — was their studio breakthrough. It is nine entirely instrumental tracks for two acoustic guitars, with Gabriela's percussive strumming doing the work of a rhythm section, and it closes with covers of Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven" and Metallica's "Orion".
albums.reception: The album debuted at number one on the Irish Albums Chart — reportedly the first instrumental album to go straight to the top there — ahead of Arctic Monkeys and Johnny Cash.

albums.blurb: Beirut is the project of Zach Condon, the Santa Fe songwriter who broke through at twenty with the Balkan-brass debut Gulag Orkestar. This second album, released in October 2007, swaps the Balkans for France — accordion, strings and flugelhorn in a chanson mode, with most of its thirteen songs named for or set in French towns. It was recorded largely in a makeshift Albuquerque studio and finished at Arcade Fire's church studio in Quebec.
albums.reception: It holds a Metacritic score of 80 out of 100, with Pitchfork rating it 8.0.

albums.blurb: Young Marble Giants were a Cardiff trio: Alison Statton's hushed, unaffected vocals over Stuart Moxham's choppy guitar and organ and Philip Moxham's melodic bass, with pre-recorded beats from a homemade drum machine in place of a kit. Colossal Youth, released on Rough Trade in February 1980, was their only studio album — a deliberate whisper against post-punk's noise — and the band split up the following year. The Spotify link is the 40th-anniversary edition, which carries the original album up front.
albums.reception: It peaked at number three on the UK Independent Albums chart, and Kurt Cobain later named it one of the ten most influential records he had ever heard.
